sovereign_territory: The Ouroboros Ring — a continuous sovereign energy corridor running the full 500-kilometer length of GLMZ, encompassing all primary power transmission infrastructure, the Lake Michigan Thermal Array (submerged geothermal and thermal differential generation), and six fusion micro-reactor clusters designated as sovereign Ouroboros installations
founding_story: Ouroboros was not founded so much as consolidated. In 2135, the GLMZ corridor experienced the Blackout Cascade — a seventeen-day total grid failure caused by simultaneous cyberattacks on fragmented municipal power authorities. When the lights came back on, energy attorney and infrastructure speculator Yael Ostrander had quietly purchased the debt and operating licenses of eleven collapsed municipal power entities during the chaos. Over the following decade, she merged, acquired, and in two cases simply absorbed smaller energy providers until Ouroboros controlled the complete generational and transmission backbone of the corridor. Ostrander declared energy sovereignty in 2146, converting her holdings into a formal corponation-state and establishing the legal precedent that power transmission infrastructure constitutes 'vital sovereign territory' under the Corporate Reclamation Acts. She died in 2151 under circumstances officially ruled accidental; the corponation she left behind is run by a board that has maintained her expansion philosophy with mechanical precision.
security_force: The Current — a 12,000-person grid protection and power-denial warfare unit. The Current specializes in infrastructure defense, electromagnetic pulse operations, and the deployment of 'brownout protocols' — controlled, targeted power reduction to specific sectors as a coercive measure. They are the only known private security force with a dedicated EMP artillery division.
key_detail: Ouroboros's closed-loop billing system — the PowerBond — automatically deducts energy costs directly from residents' and corponations' financial accounts with no opt-out mechanism. Failure to maintain a positive PowerBond balance results in immediate, automated power termination. The corponation has shut off power to three rival corponation facilities and forty residential sectors in the past five years for non-payment, each time framing it as a 'routine contract enforcement action.'
relationship_to_big_20: Ranked 3rd in the Big 20 by valuation. Widely considered one of the two or three entities that could theoretically destabilize the entire corridor if it chose to. Every other corponation in the Big 20 pays Ouroboros energy fees and is therefore structurally dependent on it. The relationship is one of deep mutual resentment and absolute practical necessity.
full_text: OUROBOROS ENERGY & CLOSED-LOOP POWER SOVEREIGNTY, INC-S — stock designation OES-I — is the dominant energy generation and grid infrastructure corponation of the GLMZ corridor and one of the three most powerful sovereign corporate entities in the megacity by any meaningful measure. Controlling the complete primary power transmission backbone of the 500-kilometer corridor, six fusion micro-reactor clusters, and the Lake Michigan Thermal Array — a submerged geothermal and thermal differential generation installation of enormous output — Ouroboros is the literal source of light, heat, and operational power for an estimated 40 million residents and hundreds of corporate entities. The corponation traces its origins to attorney Yael Ostrander's opportunistic acquisition of eleven collapsed municipal power authorities during the 2135 Blackout Cascade, a consolidation strategy she executed with cold precision over the following decade before declaring energy sovereignty in 2146. Ouroboros's PowerBond automated billing system represents one of the most criticized mechanisms in the corridor's corporate landscape — a non-optional, direct-debit infrastructure that terminates power to non-paying entities without human review or appeal process. The corponation's security arm, The Current, enforces grid sovereignty through infrastructure defense and the unique capability for targeted power denial, deploying brownout and blackout protocols as instruments of corporate coercion with chilling regularity. Valued at Φ4.7 trillion with annual revenues of Φ780 billion, Ouroboros employs 67,000 direct staff and 310,000 contracted grid workers. Ranked 3rd in the Big 20, it occupies a structural position of near-total leverage over the corridor's entire economic ecosystem — every entity that consumes power is, in a functional sense, an Ouroboros dependent.
